text: The Fed just hiked rates to 4.00–4.25% with another possible in December, while inflation is stuck at 3.4% and jobs came in hot at 162K — this means borrowing costs are rising again, which is bad news for unprofitable and speculative growth stocks in your portfolio.

Trim MSTR while you still have a small 5% gain — it's essentially a leveraged Bitcoin bet that's 57% off its high with terrible relative strength, and rising rates work against this kind of speculative position.
Trim NCLP.L because it's your largest ETF holding, down 25% and your worst-performing ETF by far, sitting well below its 50-day average with weak technicals that suggest more downside risk.
Raise your BMNR stop from $20.19 to $21.33 — this locks in a tighter safety net on a stock that's 58% off its high, so if it keeps falling you'll get out with less damage.

Consider adding to UNH — it's a best-in-class healthcare company trading at a cheap 16x earnings with nearly 12% revenue growth, and defensive healthcare tends to hold up well when rates are rising and the economy is uncertain.
